input.quote: Licenses. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, to Research, Develop, Manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise Commercialize and exploit Products
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sanofi, so it meets the preferred position. All exclusivity runs in our favour: Section 3.1 grants Sanofi an exclusive licence (even as to RevMed) and an exclusive option, and Section 13.2(q) is a RevMed warranty that no third-party exclusivity limits our rights. On sourcing, Article VII gives Sanofi oversight of Registrational/commercial Manufacture, requires RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How on request and to support Sanofi in establishing its own third-party supply agreements (Section 7.2); Section 7.3 only requires good-faith negotiation of a Supply Agreement where one Party in fact manufactures for the other, with no requirements/sole-source commitment. Noted but not flagged: Section 12.2(d) gives RevMed a termination right if Sanofi develops a Competing Product without having commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, subject to a Sanofi election to cure — that is a conditional termination right rather than an exclusive-dealing covenant restricting our freedom to source or develop, and it is standard in a collaboration of this type. No redline proposed.
